solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: An urge to see bad speller lose head

indicators.note: losing its head means the opening letter of the word for the bad speller is dropped

parts.note: a witch is someone who casts evil spells, a bad speller in the cryptic sense

explanation.surface: Someone with poor spelling is told to get rid of a desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speller' is not about spelling words but about casting spells.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving or desire for something.

clue.text: Accuses exercises after one man starts and feels pain

indicators.note: after means the exercises come behind the one-man letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: starts picks the first letter of man

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
aches means feels pain

explanation.surface: A man exercises and then feels sore, while blaming others.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach is to charge a public official with misconduct, so to accuse formally.

clue.text: Animal races covered by Herald

indicators.note: covered by means the races sit inside the herald word

parts.note: a crier, as in town crier, is a herald making announcements
TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle races

explanation.surface: A newspaper called the Herald reports on animal racing.
explanation.walkthrough: Herald looks like a newspaper title but is a town crier.
explanation.definitionFit: Critter is an informal American word for any animal or creature.

clue.text: Small amount of vintage wine set before doctor

indicators.note: set before tells us the wine comes ahead of the doctor in the answer

parts.note: a cru is a classified French vineyard or its wine
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A tiny measure of fine wine is placed in front of a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumb is a tiny fragment, so a small amount of something.

clue.text: Source of irony in angry worker's breakfast?

indicators.note: in places the source letter inside the angry word

parts.note: cross means angry

indicators.note: source of gives the first letter of irony

parts.note: an ant is a worker in crossword convention, and the 's is a link

explanation.surface: An ironic touch appears in a furious employee's morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a flaky pastry eaten at breakfast, an example of a breakfast item, as the question mark admits.

clue.text: Be disconcerting to a Parisian, never being wrong

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say

indicators.note: being wrong shows the letters of never are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is never mistaken, which is unsettling.
explanation.definitionFit: To unnerve someone is to disconcert them and sap their confidence.

clue.text: Sailors in revolutionary vessel destroyed by fire

indicators.note: in places the sailors inside the vessel
revolutionary means turned round, so the vessel word is reversed

parts.note: a tub is a vessel or container
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: Seamen aboard a rebel ship see it lost to flames.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt means damaged or consumed by fire.

clue.text: Bread and sugar

definitions.meaning: a shaped mass of baked bread
a moulded cone of sugar, as in sugarloaf

explanation.definitionFit: Both bread and refined sugar have traditionally been made in the shaped mass called by this word.

clue.text: Those mile runs — makes you supple!

indicators.note: runs, like dye running, signals the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Running those miles keeps you limber.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithesome is a variant of lissom, meaning lithe and flexible.

clue.text: A supporter welcomes almost affluent continental

indicators.note: welcomes means the supporter word takes in the other letters

parts.note: a fan is a supporter

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: rich means affluent

explanation.surface: A fan greets a nearly wealthy European visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the continent of Africa is African, so continental in that sense.

clue.text: Line beyond which investments yield nothing?

definitions.text: Line beyond which investments yield nothing?

parts.words: Line beyond which investments yield nothing?
parts.note: read as finance, a threshold past which money put in brings back no profit; the familiar phrase means the stage after which turning back is impossible

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a stage past which retreat is impossible, here punned as a point giving no financial yield.

clue.text: A fellow's first short, short and sweet

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word fellow's
short here means cut off at the end, losing the final letter

parts.note: terse means brief or short

explanation.surface: Some man's first effort is brief, curt and pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'short' is the shortening signal; the second gives TERSE, which loses its E to make TERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Afters is British slang for dessert, the sweet course after the main meal.

clue.text: Make economies, and ditch engineers first

indicators.note: first says the engineers' letters go at the front

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a trench is a ditch dug in the ground

explanation.surface: Someone is told to cut costs and get rid of the engineers before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' looks like a verb meaning get rid of, but it is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrench is to cut back spending, which is making economies.

clue.text: Their changes add years of tradition

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the word their are rearranged

parts.note: an age is a long period of years

explanation.surface: Their alterations add years of custom to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Heritage is what is handed down from the past, the inherited customs that make up a tradition.

clue.text: Translate Latin 'cedi' to yield 'the very same'

indicators.note: translate here means change the form of the letters, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A student is asked to render a Latin word into English with an exact match.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means exactly alike, the very same thing.

clue.text: Murmuring 'Money holds nothing before golf!'

indicators.note: before puts the money-and-nothing unit ahead of the golf letter
holds shows the money word wraps round the nothing

parts.note: coin is metal money
O, the figure zero, means nothing
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone mutters that cash contains nothing before a round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooing is the soft murmuring sound of doves, or of tender talk.

clue.text: Prisoner with record of French uprising modified behaviour

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
form is a criminal record in slang

indicators.note: uprising means read upwards, so the French word is reversed in this down clue

parts.note: de is French for of

explanation.surface: A convict with a history of French revolt changed his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Form is British slang for a criminal record.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to change one's behaviour to fit the rules, so conformed means modified behaviour.

clue.text: Big support for stars

parts.note: great means big
to bear is to support a weight

explanation.surface: Strong backing is given to celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation Ursa Major, containing the Plough, is known by this name for its pattern of stars.

clue.text: The way chestnut, say, is straddled by heartless sergeant

indicators.note: straddled by means the tree sits between the remaining letters of the sergeant
heartless means the inner letters of sergeant are removed, leaving the outer ones

parts.note: a chestnut is an example of a tree, as the 'say' signals

explanation.surface: A chestnut is sat astride by a sergeant who lacks compassion, on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' suggests a cruel sergeant but leaves only S and T, which straddle TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a road or way in a town.

clue.text: Outlet serving hot pears stewed with no end of sugar?

indicators.note: stewed means the letters are cooked up into a new order
end of picks the last letter of sugar, which is left out of the mix

explanation.surface: A shop sells hot stewed pears without any sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' says the sugar's last letter is removed from the pool before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A teashop is a small retail outlet serving tea and light food.

clue.text: Ship that is carrying good things to wear

indicators.note: carrying means the ship-and-that-is unit holds the letter for good inside it

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship
ie is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A vessel is said to be transporting fine clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear and nightclothes, so items worn on the body.

clue.text: Party girl dunking digestive vacantly in coffee

indicators.note: dunking puts the biscuit letters down into the coffee
in confirms the biscuit letters go inside the coffee

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

indicators.note: vacantly means emptied, leaving only the outer letters of digestive

explanation.surface: A partygoer dunks a digestive biscuit, absently, in her coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: A digestive is a British sweetmeal biscuit; emptied it leaves DE. A ladette is a young woman who behaves boisterously like the lads.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladette is British slang for a rowdy young woman who parties hard.

clue.text: Sally's fencing skill?

definitions.meaning: a sally is a witty retort, and the 's is a link meaning is
in fencing this is a quick return thrust after parrying

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a quick witty reply and a fencer's counter-thrust after a parry.

clue.text: Sustenance allowed during Lent?

parts.note: Lent is a period of fasting, so the food permitted then could jokingly be called food for a fast; the phrase really means quick takeaway meals

explanation.definitionFit: Quick takeaway meals such as burgers are known by this phrase, punned here as food for a religious fast.

clue.text: Looked on girl's love, expecting doubt initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of the words in front of it

explanation.surface: Someone watched a girl's lover, anticipating suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looked on' reads as one phrase, but 'on' starts the run of initials.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at lecherously, a kind of looking with desire.

clue.text: Things produced on strike back up management, finally

parts.note: workers on strike are out

indicators.note: back means the word up is read in reverse
finally picks the last letter of management

explanation.surface: Goods made while workers strike lend support to the bosses in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Output is the amount of goods or work produced.

clue.text: Lose case — too much worried by example of 9

indicators.note: worried, in the sense of shaken about, tells us the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who loses a court case is excessively anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is AFTERS, the dessert course, of which this is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: This chocolate dessert is a classic pudding served after the main course.

clue.text: Stone circle, white, not quite complete

parts.note: O is circle-shaped

indicators.note: not quite complete means the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: pale means whitish

explanation.surface: A ring of white stones is not entirely finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a gemstone known for its play of colours.

clue.text: Fear being late, drinking last of beer

indicators.note: drinking means the late word takes in the letter

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of beer

explanation.surface: Someone is afraid of turning up late after having a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear, as noun or verb.

clue.text: One who succeeds by getting musical composition broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast signals the word is spoken out, so we hear it

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A successful person gets their piece of music played on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir succeeds to a title or property on the holder's death.
